record.paper_title: Polycyclic Codes Associated with Trinomials: Good Codes and Open Questions
record.context_brief: equivalence of code families for equal-order reciprocal-style trinomials
record.original_question: Let t1(x) = x^n - a x^i - b and t2(x) = x^n - a' x^(n-i) - b' be trinomials over a finite field F_q with the same order, meaning Ord(t1(x)) = Ord(t2(x)). If C1 is the family of all length-n polycyclic codes over F_q associated with t1(x), and C2 is the family of all length-n polycyclic codes over F_q associated with t2(x), is there always a one-to-one correspondence between C1 and C2 such that each code in one family corresponds to an equivalent code in the other family?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.5. Let t1pxq = x^n - axi - b, t2pxq = x^n - a' x^(n-i) - b' P Fq[x] be such that Ord(t1(x)) = Ord(t2(x)). Let C1 be the set of all polycyclic codes of length n over Fq associated with t1(x) and C2 be the set of all polycyclic codes of length n over Fq associated with t2(x). Then C1 and C2 are in a one-to-one correspondence where corresponding codes are equivalent to each other.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{F}_q$ be a finite field with $q$ elements, and fix integers $n \geq 2$ and $1 \leq i \leq n-1$. For a monic polynomial $f(x) \in \mathbb{F}_q[x]$ of degree $n$, a polycyclic code of length $n$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$ associated with $f(x)$ is, by definition, an ideal of the quotient ring $\mathbb{F}_q[x]/\langle f(x)\rangle$, viewed as an $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear subspace of $\mathbb{F}_q^n$ via the natural identification $(c_0,c_1,\dots,c_{n-1}) \leftrightarrow c_0 + c_1 x + \cdots + c_{n-1} x^{n-1}$. Two linear codes $C, C' \subseteq \mathbb{F}_q^n$ are called equivalent if there exists a monomial transformation (a permutation of coordinates composed with multiplication of each coordinate by a nonzero scalar) that maps $C$ onto $C'$. For a polynomial $f(x) \in \mathbb{F}_q[x]$ with $f(0) \neq 0$, the order $\operatorname{Ord}(f(x))$ is the least positive integer $e$ such that $f(x) \mid x^e - 1$ in $\mathbb{F}_q[x]$.

Consider two trinomials
$$t_1(x) = x^n - a x^i - b, \qquad t_2(x) = x^n - a' x^{\,n-i} - b'$$
in $\mathbb{F}_q[x]$, with $a,b,a',b' \in \mathbb{F}_q^\times$, and assume $\operatorname{Ord}(t_1(x)) = \operatorname{Ord}(t_2(x))$. Let $\mathcal{C}_1$ denote the set of all polycyclic codes of length $n$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$ associated with $t_1(x)$, and let $\mathcal{C}_2$ denote the analogous set for $t_2(x)$.

Prove or disprove: there always exists a bijection $\Phi : \mathcal{C}_1 \to \mathcal{C}_2$ such that for every $C \in \mathcal{C}_1$, the code $\Phi(C)$ is equivalent to $C$.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is stated as a conjecture in work on polycyclic codes associated with trinomials. Follow-up literature on skew polycyclic codes (e.g., a 2025 preprint on bounds and equivalence of skew polycyclic codes) discusses equivalence of trinomial-defined ambient spaces but does not appear to resolve this specific conjecture in the commutative setting. No published proof or counterexample was located, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Polycyclic codes associated with trinomials: good codes and open questions
status_evidence.snippet: Several properties of trinomial codes and a number of conjectures related to their equivalence and duality are presented.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture on one-to-one correspondence between code families is stated as an open question in the published version.

status_evidence.title: Bounds and Equivalence of Skew Polycyclic Codes over Finite Fields
status_evidence.snippet: Equivalence of ambient spaces for skew polycyclic codes... general conditions under which two such ambient spaces yield equivalent code families.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work addresses equivalence in the skew setting but does not resolve the commutative trinomial conjecture.
